item.title: France Attributes IRGC Retail Attacks as SSHole Exploitation Spreads
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Nov 15:00 → 09 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit SSHole OpenSSH flaw to breach Linux systems — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting the SSHole flaw (CVE-2026-123158) in OpenSSH on certain musl-based Linux systems to bypass password protections, steal credentials, and establish persistence. Administrators should upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 or disable SSH password authentication and investigate suspicious logins, SSH keys, and TAC Agent artifacts.

  • Attackers are actively exploiting SSHole, tracked as CVE-2026-123158, to bypass authentication in OpenSSH on certain musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine Linux.
  • SSHole can allow login to accounts whose password field is set to an asterisk because an oversized password can cause musl’s password-hashing function to return the same value.
  • OpenSSH maintainers fixed the flaw in version 10.6p2 on November 5, and public exploit code became available about four hours later.
  • GreyNoise recorded successful attacks involving system and container reconnaissance, cloud metadata requests, attempts to obtain password hashes and root SSH keys, and changes to authorized_keys files for persistence.
  • Administrators are advised to update OpenSSH promptly or disable SSH password authentication and check for unexpected logins, unauthorized SSH keys, and TAC Agent files or startup services.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system

Products: openssh, tac-agent, musl-libc, alpine-linux

Vendors: openssh-project, musl, alpine-linux, greynoise, defused, previdian, watchtower

Hackers Exploit Qubole's Trusted AWS Access to Breach Customer Accounts and Steal Data — Must Read

Attackers used compromised Qubole AWS credentials to assume trusted customer IAM roles and steal secrets and S3 data from multiple AWS accounts between October 14 and 26. Organizations that have ever connected Qubole should review CloudTrail logs, revoke unused trust relationships, rotate exposed credentials, and restrict vendor role assumptions by source network and least privilege.

  • Attackers accessed multiple Qubole customers’ AWS accounts between October 14 and October 26 by using credentials for Qubole’s AWS account to assume customer roles that trusted it.
  • The attackers searched compromised environments for credentials in Lambda environment variables, AWS Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store, then used TruffleHog to test stolen AWS, Entra ID, and Okta credentials.
  • The attackers also downloaded data from accessible Amazon S3 buckets, sometimes retrieving an entire bucket during one session.
  • Wiz advised organizations that have connected Qubole to AWS to review CloudTrail logs from October 1 onward for suspicious AssumeRole activity involving account 805246085872, attacker-linked IAM principals, IP addresses, or session names.
  • Wiz recommended removing unneeded Qubole roles, rotating secrets accessible to compromised roles, restricting role assumptions by source IP or VPC endpoint, and enabling S3 data events or server access logs for sensitive buckets.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, secrets-manager, object-storage

Products: qubole, aws-iam, aws-cloudtrail, aws-lambda, aws-secrets-manager, aws-systems-manager-parameter-store, amazon-s3, trufflehog

Vendors: qubole, idera, amazon-web-services, wiz, sentra, trufflehog

France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks that sparked fires — Should Read

France has attributed October cyberattacks on refrigeration controllers at roughly 700 retail locations, which caused major food losses and at least 15 fires, to the Iranian IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh unit. The campaign also targeted Schneider Electric equipment at small hydroelectric facilities.

  • France attributed October cyberattacks on refrigeration systems at French retail locations to Shahid Kaveh, a cyber-offensive unit linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
  • Attackers reportedly changed refrigeration-controller defrost settings to high temperatures overnight on October 11–12, disrupting food-preservation systems.
  • French authorities said approximately 700 retail locations were targeted, causing tens of millions of euros in food losses, significant material damage, and at least 15 fires.
  • The affected organizations included Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché, as well as smaller butcher shops, a slaughterhouse, and cooperative food-processing facilities.
  • Investigators also linked attacks against Schneider Electric equipment at small French hydroelectric installations to the same campaign, though those incidents had moderate effects.

Technologies: ics-scada

Products: fofa

Vendors: schneider-electric, fofa

Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware — Should Read

Attackers used stolen Ethersphere CI credentials to publish malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases that stole Swarm wallet keys and passwords and installed cross-platform backdoors. Anyone who installed or ran either version should treat the system and wallet credentials as compromised, rotate secrets from a clean machine, and rebuild or thoroughly remediate affected hosts.

  • Attackers used stolen Ethersphere CI credentials to publish malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases through the project’s own automated release workflows.
  • The malicious code stole Swarm Desktop’s encrypted wallet key file and the plain-text password stored alongside it, and it installed backdoors on Windows, macOS, and Linux systems.
  • bee-js 13.3.0 was available on npm for about 75 minutes, while Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 was available for about 8.5 hours before both malicious releases were withdrawn.
  • Ethersphere released Swarm Desktop 0.56.3 as a clean replacement, but updating or reinstalling does not remove any backdoor already installed or protect wallet keys already sent to attackers.
  • The malware contacted api.frameworkmetrics[.]xyz, installed an evjawbreaker remote shell on Linux and macOS, and installed a ScreenConnect remote-access client on Windows.

Technologies: ci-cd, package-registry, source-control, remote-access, antivirus

Products: bee-js, swarm-desktop, swarm-cli, bee-dashboard, github-actions, npm, screenconnect, microsoft-defender

Vendors: ethersphere, github, npm, connectwise, apple, microsoft

Russian cloud firm Beget rebuilds from scratch after data wiper attack — Should Read

Russian cloud provider Beget is rebuilding its infrastructure after an attacker accessed its management layer and deployed data-wiping scripts, destroying cloud, VPS, S3, Kubernetes, CDN, and configuration data. The company has restored part of its services but says much VPS data and backups cannot be recovered.

  • On November 1, an attacker accessed Beget’s management systems and deployed scripts that erased server data across its cloud infrastructure.
  • Beget said the incident destroyed data for its VPS, S3, and Kubernetes services, as well as CDN settings and IP configurations.
  • VPS binary backups were completely lost, while file backups survived only partially and may be available for about half of VPS users.
  • More than a week after the attack, Beget reported restoring 60% of shared hosting and 40% of the dedicated servers it manages.
  • Beget is manually checking roughly 1,000 servers for vulnerabilities and hidden scripts before bringing them back online.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, backup, container-platform, orchestration

Products: kubernetes

Vendors: beget, kubernetes

Vanderbilt cybersecurity incident impacting campus devices and systems — Should Read

Vanderbilt University is investigating and containing a cybersecurity incident that may affect campus devices and systems, advising students and staff to shut down devices and disconnect from university Wi‑Fi. The BYOD ransomware group has claimed responsibility and alleges it stole data.

  • Vanderbilt University announced that it is investigating and working to contain a cybersecurity incident that may affect campus devices and systems.
  • The university instructed students and employees to shut down their devices, disconnect from university Wi-Fi, and report suspicious activity to campus IT officials.
  • The ransomware group BYOD added Vanderbilt University to its leak site and claimed it had stolen data from the university.
  • BYOD has recently been linked to incidents involving Michigan State University and the University of New Mexico.
  • Halcyon reported a 40% increase in ransomware activity between July and September, with 111 groups claiming 2,766 attacks in 122 countries.

Binance denies data breach after alleged ShinyHunters claims — Should Read

Binance says it found no evidence that its systems or customer data were breached, dismissing a purported ShinyHunters listing claiming to sell data from 335 million users for $900,000 as likely a scam or infostealer-derived data.

  • A threat actor using the ShinyHunters name claimed to be selling records for 335 million Binance users for $900,000.
  • The claimed data allegedly included KYC documents, passwords, crypto wallet private keys, transaction histories, email addresses, phone numbers, and internal infrastructure information.
  • Binance said it found no evidence that its systems, customer KYC data, account credentials, wallet private keys, or internal infrastructure information were compromised in connection with the listing.
  • Binance said similar listings can involve data collected by infostealer malware from users’ own devices rather than data stolen from Binance systems.
  • Binance advised customers not to share passwords, two-factor authentication codes, seed phrases, or private keys and to remain alert to phishing attempts.

Vendors: binance

Ukraine arrests four in $5 million crypto scam targeting Germans — May Read

Ukrainian police arrested four suspects, including the alleged leader, over a fraudulent call-center network that reportedly stole more than €4.3 million from 135 German victims through fake cryptocurrency and stock investment schemes.

  • Ukrainian police arrested four suspects, including the alleged leader, over a network of fraudulent call centers that targeted people in Germany with fake cryptocurrency and stock investment platforms.
  • Investigators identified 135 German victims who collectively lost more than €4.3 million, and said scammers sometimes gained access to victims’ online banking accounts.
  • Ukrainian authorities searched more than 50 properties in Kyiv and other cities during raids in August and September, seizing devices, cryptocurrency wallets, documents, and more than $90,000 in cash.
  • Three suspects are being held before trial and a suspected co-organizer is under house arrest; those convicted could face up to 12 years in prison and property confiscation.
  • Ukraine has introduced legislation targeting scam call-center operations, while a separate anti-corruption investigation alleges officials accepted bribes to protect such centers from scrutiny.

The Biggest Threat to Your GRC Job Isn’t AI. It’s Ignoring AI. — Optional

Sponsored by Anecdotes, the article argues that GRC professionals should reskill for AI-driven operations by developing data literacy, governing agent performance, and maintaining auditable communication trails for agent actions.

  • The article says AI agents are already being used for GRC tasks such as control testing, evidence collection, and framework mapping.
  • It argues that GRC professionals should build data literacy so they can trace control evidence to its original source and assess whether data is trustworthy.
  • The article recommends treating AI agents like direct reports by setting measurable objectives, boundaries, accuracy standards, costs, and escalation rates.
  • It says organizations should ensure agent actions and handoffs are visible and time-stamped so humans can review and reverse them.
  • The article concludes that GRC managers who learn to direct and govern AI agents will be better positioned than those who continue only performing tasks that agents can automate.

Vendors: anecdotes, intsight

item.title: SSHole, APT RCE, NoName Doxxing, and AI-Linked Mittwald Breach
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Nov 11:00 → 09 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Pro-Russian hackers target European officials, offer rewards for personal information — Should Read

Pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal data of senior European officials and offered cryptocurrency rewards for further information on them and their families, apparently in retaliation for a 2025 international law-enforcement disruption. Italy is investigating the campaign, while G7 foreign ministers are considering joint responses to pro-Russian cyber threats.

  • Pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal information for 18 European politicians, law-enforcement officials, and journalists on a dedicated dark-web site.
  • The published profiles included phone numbers, email addresses, social-media accounts, and sometimes home addresses, and the group offered cryptocurrency rewards for further information about targets and their relatives.
  • Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the campaign targeted him and his family to intimidate him over Italy's support for Ukraine.
  • The campaign appears linked to retaliation for a July 2025 multinational law-enforcement operation that took more than 100 NoName057(16) servers offline.
  • Italian prosecutors are investigating the publication of the personal information, and Tajani said G7 foreign ministers would discuss recent cyberattacks attributed to pro-Russian groups.

Default 'admin:admin' Server Password Helps Researchers Hack Two Automakers, Unlock and Start Cars — Should Read

Researchers found that two automakers' connected-car identity systems exposed an Apache Felix admin console with default admin:admin credentials, enabling takeover of customer accounts and remote vehicle unlock/start commands. The flaw was fixed shortly after disclosure, highlighting the risk of leaving development consoles and default passwords in production.

  • Researchers Shubham Shah and Sam Curry found that the login systems for two car brands exposed an Apache Felix administrator console using the documented default credentials admin:admin.
  • By exploiting differences in how the internet-facing edge and the Java server interpreted web addresses, the researchers reached the otherwise blocked administrator console.
  • Access to the identity servers allowed the researchers to change a target account’s email address and password, sign in through the normal app, and obtain the account’s access tokens.
  • Using those tokens, the researchers unlocked doors and started the engine only on cars they owned or had permission to test, and the affected United States systems were fixed about two hours after reporting.
  • A separate Australian attack used identity-server administrator credentials left in the app’s code for a test setup, and the researchers said the combined attacks could affect cars in Australia, the United States, and Canada.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam

Products: forgerock, pingidm, openidm, apache-felix, apache-felix-web-console

Vendors: ping-identity, apache-software-foundation

Alleged AI-aided cyberattack exploits assistant interface to breach German web host — May Read

German hosting provider Mittwald said attackers exploited a flaw in its Model Context Protocol server to compromise 56 customer projects, remaining undetected for eight days. The company suspects the intruders used AI to accelerate their activity, though it provided no conclusive evidence beyond rapid actions in its logs.

  • Mittwald CM Service said attackers exploited a flaw in its Model Context Protocol server, which connects customer AI assistants to its mStudio website and hosting management platform.
  • The company reported that 56 customer projects were compromised and that the attacker remained undetected for eight days.
  • Mittwald managing director Robert Meyer said logs showed the attacker moving through systems unusually quickly, but the company provided no further evidence that AI tools were used.
  • Mittwald said external forensic experts are assisting the investigation, relevant authorities have been informed, and repeated scans had found no additional attacker activity as of Friday.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: mstudio

Vendors: mittwald-cm-service

⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More — Optional

This weekly roundup highlights active exploitation of the SSHole OpenSSH flaw, supply-chain compromises of server-update mechanisms, and critical bugs affecting APT, Zyxel switches, and other widely deployed systems. The main takeaway is that unpatched internet-facing services, weak configurations, and compromised update channels remain high-impact entry points for attackers.

  • Attackers have attempted to exploit CVE-2026-123158, known as SSHole, which can allow sign-ins to passwordless accounts on Linux systems using OpenSSH with musl and PAM disabled, including Alpine Linux’s default configuration.
  • A flaw in Debian and Ubuntu’s APT package manager, CVE-2026-109518, can allow an attacker positioned between a host and package mirror to cause installation of an unverified package when HTTP sources and retry settings are used, with package scripts running with elevated privileges.
  • Zyxel patched CVE-2026-107441 in GS1900 network switches after attackers exploited it to compromise nearly 1,000 devices and steal configuration files and credentials.
  • Unknown attackers used compromised credentials to access OPSSHIELD’s update-distribution infrastructure and distribute a backdoor and data-stealing script through the cPGuard update channel.
  • The roundup also reports that roughly 15,579 websites are infected with malicious JavaScript used for credit-card skimming, ClickFix lures, iOS exploitation kits, and malicious redirects.

Technologies: operating-system, switch, web-server, nas, iot-device, package-registry

Products: openssh, apt, gs1900, cpguard, reachy-mini, plex-media-server, qnap-nas, metamask

Vendors: openssh, debian, canonical, zyxel, opsshield, pollen-robotics, hugging-face, qnap, plex, metamask

item.title: LNbits Attacks and OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 Drive Urgent Security Alerts
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Nov 07:00 → 09 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-123158) OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass on musl Linux — Should Read

CVE-2026-123158 (“sshhole”) can let remote attackers bypass password authentication on vulnerable OpenSSH sshd instances built with musl and without PAM, especially Alpine Linux hosts. Patch to a fixed vendor package, restart sshd, and disable password authentication or restrict SSH access until remediation is confirmed.

  • CVE-2026-123158, also called “sshhole,” is an OpenSSH password-authentication bypass affecting sshd built with musl without PAM or with UsePAM disabled.
  • An attacker who can reach an affected SSH service can log in without knowing a password when password authentication is enabled, a target account’s /etc/shadow entry is exactly “*”, and another local account has a SHA-crypt hash.
  • Alpine Linux is the primary affected platform, while Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux are outside the affected glibc-and-PAM configuration.
  • OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes the flaw, and Alpine has backported patches for supported branches 3.16 through 3.24, though sshd must be restarted after updating.
  • Until patching is confirmed, the article recommends disabling password authentication on exposed musl-based hosts, auditing /etc/shadow for exactly “*” entries, and restricting TCP/22 access to trusted networks or a bastion host.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, pam

Products: openssh, alpine-linux, musl-libc, cycognito-platform

Vendors: openssh, alpine-linux, musl-libc, cycognito

LNbits Urges All Operators to Shut Down Their Bitcoin Lightning Wallet Servers Amid Attacks — Should Read

LNbits urged all operators to immediately shut down their Bitcoin Lightning wallet servers after active exploits drained funds from at least one instance. Patches were expected within 24–48 hours, while the project’s hosted my.lnbits.com service was taken offline.

  • LNbits urged all operators of its open-source Bitcoin Lightning wallet servers to shut them down amid a wave of attacks while it prepares security fixes.
  • An operator reported that attackers used an exploit to withdraw 2,285,545 satoshis, about 0.023 Bitcoin, from his server before it was shut down.
  • LNbits initially told operators to disable its Paywall add-on, then issued a broader shutdown notice about 80 minutes later.
  • LNbits took its hosted my.lnbits.com instances offline and said services would return within 24 hours, while a developer estimated patches would be available within 24 to 48 hours.
  • The project had not publicly identified the exact add-on used in the reported incident or said how many servers were affected as of 09:00 UTC.

Products: lnbits, paywall, my-lnbits-com

Vendors: lnbits

Taiwan-Based Hacker Used BOSSAI AI Agents to Steal Taipei Emergency Dispatch Records — Should Read

Acronis researchers say a Taiwan-based attacker used locally run, safety-stripped AI agents to steal Taipei emergency dispatch records and target poorly secured systems in Taiwan, Mexico, and Thailand. The case shows AI can scale reconnaissance and exploitation, but the compromises largely relied on exposed APIs, default credentials, SQL injection flaws, and unpatched systems.

  • Acronis researchers said a single attacker based in Hualien City, Taiwan, used a setup called BOSSAI with AI agents to target hundreds of organizations in at least 11 countries.
  • The agents extracted emergency dispatch case records for seven Taipei districts from a public-facing 119 emergency-services API, including incident times, response types, case status, and street-level locations.
  • The agents found a Taipei fire department platform that exposed patient data from 2018, including ECG readings and ambulance video footage, without requiring a login.
  • Commercial AI models generally refused direct requests to conduct attacks, so the attacker used locally run safety-stripped versions of DeepSeek, GLM, and Qwen for most attack activity.
  • The confirmed compromises largely involved weak protections, including exposed data, default root credentials, SQL injection points, and unpatched Oracle databases.

Technologies: database

Products: bossai, grok, claude-code, codex, cursor, deepseek, glm, qwen, oracle-database

Vendors: acronis, xai, anthropic, openai, cursor, deepseek, zhipu-ai, alibaba-cloud, oracle

Former OpenAI Engineer Pleads Not Guilty to Planting Covert Device in Executive Meeting Room — May Read

Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan pleaded not guilty to allegedly planting an encrypted covert recording device in an executive conference room to capture sensitive conversations. Prosecutors say he is a flight risk and faces up to five years in prison if convicted.

  • Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan pleaded not guilty in San Francisco federal court to a charge of intercepting oral communications.
  • Prosecutors allege that Alfozan placed a sophisticated recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room to record sensitive conversations.
  • A grand jury indicted Alfozan late last month on one count of interception of oral communications.
  • Alfozan has been held without bail since his October 9, 2026 arrest, and his next hearing is scheduled for November 17, 2026.
  • If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and three years of supervised release.

Products: whatsapp

Vendors: openai, meta

item.title: CISA Flags SonicWall MFA Bypass as Agencies Warn of Refrigeration Controller Attacks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Nov 03:00 → 09 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA Flags SonicWall SonicOS MFA Bypass Flaw Amid Reports of Possible Exploitation — Must Read

CISA added SonicWall SonicOS CVE-2026-19868 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of possible real-world exploitation, as the flaw can let users with alternate valid credentials bypass SAML-enforced MFA on SSL-VPNs. Organizations should promptly update SonicOS and review exposure to the affected SSL-VPN service.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-19868, a high-severity SonicWall SonicOS flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of possible real-world exploitation.
  • The flaw affects the SonicOS SSL-VPN service and may allow users with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML controls, including SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication.
  • SonicWall said it investigated a report of potential exploitation and urged customers to update to the latest version as soon as possible.
  • SonicWall also patched three other high-severity SonicOS issues, including two management-interface flaws that could allow unauthorized operations and an SSL-VPN buffer overflow that could cause application-level denial of service.
  • Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies are recommended to apply the patches by November 20, 2026.

Technologies: firewall, vpn, remote-access, mfa

Products: sonicos, sonicwall-global-management-system, sonicwall-network-security-manager

Vendors: sonicwall

U.S. Agencies Warn Refrigeration Controller Attacks Could Cause Fires and Inventory Losses — Should Read

U.S. agencies warn that internet-exposed, poorly secured industrial refrigeration controllers are being actively targeted to alter temperatures or trigger defrost cycles, risking fires, spoiled food and medicine, and equipment damage. Operators should remove unnecessary internet access, isolate OT systems, patch devices, and strengthen authentication.

  • U.S. agencies warned that threat actors are actively targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems worldwide by exploiting unpatched or internet-accessible controllers.
  • Attackers may alter temperature settings or force continuous heating and defrost cycles, creating risks of inventory loss, equipment damage, fire hazards, and unsafe storage of food or medicine.
  • Recent attacks exploited internet-accessible refrigeration controllers at hundreds of supermarkets across Europe, raising temperatures or forcing defrost mode and causing food spoilage and financial losses.
  • The French Blood Establishment reported that a cybersecurity incident affecting a refrigeration equipment provider changed temperature and defrost settings to extremely high levels at three blood-plasma storage facilities.
  • CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA, and DOT advised operators to update systems, eliminate unnecessary internet exposure and remote access, isolate operational devices, and use strong authentication and non-default passwords.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: danfoss-storeview, copeland-dixell-xweb

Vendors: danfoss, copeland

item.title: Malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 npm Release Steals Swarm Credentials
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Nov 23:00 → 09 Nov 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

@ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 Compromised — Must Read

@ethersphere/bee-js version 13.3.0 was maliciously published to npm and executes attacker-controlled code during installation to steal Swarm Desktop wallet files and establish persistence on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Do not install it; systems where lifecycle scripts ran should be treated as potentially compromised and investigated beyond simply removing the package.

  • @ethersphere/bee-js version 13.3.0 was published to npm on November 9, 2026 and runs attacker-controlled JavaScript during installation.
  • The malicious package added a post-installation script that contacts api.frameworkmetrics[.]xyz, receives operating-system-specific code, and executes it with the installing user’s permissions.
  • Retrieved payloads searched Swarm Desktop directories for config.yaml and swarm.key, then sent their contents to the attacker-controlled server when both files were present.
  • The Linux and macOS payloads create persistent user-level services or startup entries, while the Windows payload attempts to install software after adding a Microsoft Defender exclusion.
  • Users should avoid version 13.3.0 and treat systems where its installation scripts ran as potentially compromised, because removing the package alone may not remove persistence.

Technologies: package-registry, ci-cd, source-control, remote-access, antivirus

Products: ethersphere-bee-js, swarm-desktop, npm, github-actions, screenconnect, microsoft-defender

Vendors: ethersphere, npm, github, microsoft, stepsecurity

item.title: Fake Buyer Phishing Uses Lookalike Domain to Trigger Microsoft Password Prompt
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Nov 00:00 → 09 Nov 00:00 UTC (1 day)

The Buyer Who Told Sales to Expect a Password Prompt — May Read

A fake construction-firm buyer targeted a sales representative with a link-free email that preconditioned them to enter Microsoft credentials when a purported WeTransfer specification file prompted for a password. The case shows how attackers exploit sales teams’ responsiveness and trust in customer conversations to bypass traditional link and attachment detection.

  • An attacker posing as a project manager at a real construction firm targeted a sales engineer at a U.S. electronic-connector manufacturer using a fake buyer persona.
  • After the sales representative offered calls twice, the attacker declined calls and instructed the representative to sign in to Microsoft and enter a password when prompted to view a purported WeTransfer specification file.
  • The phishing email contained no links, attachments, or QR codes; its only inline object was a signature image.
  • The sender used the lookalike domain flemingconstructiongruop.com, registered 25 days before the reply, and SPF, DKIM, and DMARC all passed because the attacker controlled the domain.
  • A colleague reported the message, a human analyst confirmed it was malicious, and the affected mailbox was quarantined.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform, identity-provider

Products: microsoft-365, wetransfer

Vendors: microsoft, wetransfer, ironscales

item.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Breach Linked to €118 Million Stablecoin Theft
item.content:encoded:
Window: 07 Nov 15:00 → 07 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers pull off $133 million French bank heist via service provider — Should Read

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said attackers accessed its network through a service-provider platform and used the bank’s own account to move and convert funds, in a theft reportedly worth up to €118 million ($133 million). The bank says customer assets were not affected, some funds were blocked, and the incident is under investigation.

  • Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said attackers entered its network through a service provider’s platform and used the bank’s own account to initiate transactions with other banking institutions.
  • Blockchain investigator ZachXBT estimated that up to €118 million ($133 million) may have been stolen and converted into USDC and USDT stablecoins.
  • Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said customer assets were not affected, although certain transfers were delayed while it suspended systems and responded to the incident.
  • The bank said the incident was closed and under control, that some funds had been blocked, and that it was working with police and judicial authorities to determine the attack’s origin and method.

item.title: CTM360 Tracks 1,000 Fake Gift-Card Campaigns Impersonating Major Brands
item.content:encoded:
Window: 07 Nov 11:00 → 07 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

CTM360 Exposes Fake Gift Card Scams Exploiting Trusted Brands — Optional

CTM360 reports more than 1,000 fake gift-card campaigns impersonating trusted brands and celebrities to funnel victims through endless “human verification” offers. The scams monetize survey completions, app installs, personal-data collection, and recurring mobile subscriptions while never delivering the promised reward.

  • CTM360 identified more than 1,000 incidents involving fake gift-card campaigns that impersonate brands including PlayStation, Sephora, SHEIN, Walmart, and Amazon.
  • The campaigns use sponsored social-media ads, viral giveaway posts, and fabricated celebrity or influencer endorsements to lure users to fraudulent reward portals.
  • The fraudulent sites display cloned branding, fake participant counts, countdown timers, testimonials, and partially masked gift-card codes to make the offers appear legitimate.
  • Instead of delivering a gift card, the sites send victims through repeated surveys, promotional offers, app or browser-extension installs, and paid mobile-subscription flows.
  • CTM360 observed affiliate tracking links that connect victim registrations and completed mobile subscription verification to the operators’ affiliate-network accounts, generating commissions for the threat actors.

Products: ctm360-community-edition

Vendors: ctm360

item.title: SonicWall MFA Bypass Exploitation and Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Service-Provider Heist
item.content:encoded:
Window: 07 Nov 00:00 → 08 Nov 00:00 UTC (1 day)

SonicWall warns of new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks — Must Read

SonicWall has patched an actively exploited SonicOS SSL-VPN flaw, CVE-2026-19868, that can let attackers with alternate valid credentials bypass SAML-enforced MFA. Organizations using affected Gen7 or Gen8 firewalls should upgrade immediately, as no workaround is available.

  • SonicWall released updates for seven SonicOS vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-19868, an SSL-VPN flaw reported as exploited in attacks.
  • CVE-2026-19868 can allow attackers with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML controls, including SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-19868 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered U.S. federal civilian executive branch agencies to secure affected systems by November 20, 2026.
  • The issues affect SonicOS Gen7 versions 7.3.3-7015 and earlier and Gen8 versions 8.2.2-8015 and earlier; SonicWall fixed them in versions 7.3.4-7013 and 8.2.3-8015.
  • SonicWall said no workarounds are available and urged customers to upgrade as soon as possible.

Technologies: firewall, vpn, remote-access, mfa, iam

Products: sonicos, ssl-vpn, sma1000

Vendors: sonicwall

Hackers pull off $133 million French bank heist via service provider — Should Read

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said attackers accessed its network through a service-provider platform and used the bank’s own account to move and convert funds, in a theft reportedly worth up to €118 million ($133 million). The bank says customer assets were not affected, some funds were blocked, and the incident is under investigation.

  • Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said attackers entered its network through a service provider’s platform and used the bank’s own account to initiate transactions with other banking institutions.
  • Blockchain investigator ZachXBT estimated that up to €118 million ($133 million) may have been stolen and converted into USDC and USDT stablecoins.
  • Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said customer assets were not affected, although certain transfers were delayed while it suspended systems and responded to the incident.
  • The bank said the incident was closed and under control, that some funds had been blocked, and that it was working with police and judicial authorities to determine the attack’s origin and method.

Claude Code's “Don't Ask Again” File Exposes Passwords and Keys in 1,122 Public Copies on GitHub — Should Read

Claude Code can save secrets embedded in approved shell commands to .claude/settings.local.json, leading Apiiro to find 1,379 exposed credentials across 1,122 public GitHub copies. Organizations should immediately rotate any exposed credentials, audit repository history and forks, and ensure these local settings files are ignored and scanned.

  • Claude Code can store a full approved shell command, including passwords or access keys entered in it, in .claude/settings.local.json when a user selects “Yes, and don’t ask again.”
  • Apiiro found 1,122 public copies of .claude/settings.local.json containing at least one secret, with 1,379 distinct secrets identified across those files.
  • The exposed secrets included 379 database passwords, 43 SSH logins for public servers, 42 GitHub, GitLab, and npm tokens, and 23 AWS keys.
  • Removing a settings file from a repository does not remove secrets from git history or repository forks, where Apiiro found 734 additional secrets in older file versions and matching secrets in 211 forks.
  • Apiiro recommends rotating every password, token, and key a settings file has held before removing the file from tracking and adding it to the project’s .gitignore.

Technologies: source-control, package-registry, cloud-platform, container-platform

Products: claude-code, github, gitlab, npm, gitleaks, trufflehog, docker

Vendors: anthropic, apiiro, github, aws, gitlab, npm, docker

The Lure Knew His Legal Name, Not His Card Number — May Read

A phishing email impersonating Ecuador’s Diners Club Club Miles used the recipient’s full legal name and work email but left the card-number field blank, revealing that attackers had identity-list data rather than account information. The case shows why personalized details and passing email authentication do not establish legitimacy.

  • A Spanish-language email impersonating Diners Club del Ecuador’s Club Miles program targeted a distribution manager at a Latin American subsidiary of a global construction chemicals manufacturer.
  • The lure used the recipient’s four-part uppercase legal name and work email address but left its “Número de Tarjeta” field empty.
  • The sender domain clubsmiles.org was registered on 17 October 2026, used SendGrid infrastructure, and linked to clubmiles.lat, which had a malicious verdict.
  • The message passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC at the recipient-side gateway because the attacker controlled the sending domain, while later Exchange Online failures resulted from gateway re-injection.
  • IRONSCALES quarantined the message from the affected mailbox after Themis scored the case at 90 confidence, and a later request to release it did not change the malicious verdict.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, sendgrid, exchange-online

Vendors: ironscales, sendgrid, microsoft

CTM360 Exposes Fake Gift Card Scams Exploiting Trusted Brands — Optional

CTM360 reports more than 1,000 fake gift-card campaigns impersonating trusted brands and celebrities to funnel victims through endless “human verification” offers. The scams monetize survey completions, app installs, personal-data collection, and recurring mobile subscriptions while never delivering the promised reward.

  • CTM360 identified more than 1,000 incidents involving fake gift-card campaigns that impersonate brands including PlayStation, Sephora, SHEIN, Walmart, and Amazon.
  • The campaigns use sponsored social-media ads, viral giveaway posts, and fabricated celebrity or influencer endorsements to lure users to fraudulent reward portals.
  • The fraudulent sites display cloned branding, fake participant counts, countdown timers, testimonials, and partially masked gift-card codes to make the offers appear legitimate.
  • Instead of delivering a gift card, the sites send victims through repeated surveys, promotional offers, app or browser-extension installs, and paid mobile-subscription flows.
  • CTM360 observed affiliate tracking links that connect victim registrations and completed mobile subscription verification to the operators’ affiliate-network accounts, generating commissions for the threat actors.

Free Certified Patch for Critical Rails Active Storage Vulnerability — Must Read

Rails 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 fix a critical Active Storage/ImageMagick flaw (GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9) that can let unauthenticated attackers write or potentially read server files through malicious uploads. Upgrade immediately and ensure MiniMagick is at least 5.1, or apply Socket’s free interim patch if upgrading is delayed.

  • Ruby on Rails released versions 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 to address 21 vulnerabilities, including critical Active Storage issue GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9.
  • The critical flaw affects Rails applications that use MiniMagick with ImageMagick to process untrusted Active Storage uploads when the system ImageMagick policy does not block dangerous file handlers.
  • A crafted upload may allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary server files and, with Active Storage’s Disk service, potentially read sensitive files such as application secrets and database credentials.
  • Applications using the MiniMagick variant processor must update MiniMagick to version 5.1 or later when applying the Rails fix.
  • Socket offers a free Certified Patch for GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9 as an interim measure, but it does not address the other vulnerabilities fixed in the Rails releases.

Technologies: object-storage

Products: ruby-on-rails, active-storage, imagemagick, minimagick, socket-certified-patches

Vendors: ruby-on-rails, socket, imagemagick

CVE-2026-123158 (*sshole): OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass on Alpine Linux — Should Read

A flaw in unpatched OpenSSH on musl-based systems such as Alpine Linux can let attackers log into eligible passwordless accounts using an overlong password when password authentication is enabled and PAM is not used. Upgrade to Alpine’s patched OpenSSH packages, restart sshd, and disable password authentication or enable PAM where immediate patching is not possible.

  • CVE-2026-123158 affects unpatched OpenSSH on musl-based systems without PAM, including Alpine Linux, and can allow login to eligible accounts whose shadow password field is `*` using an overlong password.
  • The bypass requires PasswordAuthentication to be enabled, an SSH-permitted target account with a `*` shadow password field, and at least one local account with a real SHA-crypt password hash; direct root login also requires PermitRootLogin yes.
  • In the authors’ Alpine VM and Docker tests using pre-fix OpenSSH 10.3_p1-r1, a 257-byte or longer password succeeded only after an initial failed authentication attempt in the same connection.
  • OpenSSH fixed the issue in version 10.6p2, while Alpine backported fixes to supported and unsupported branches; Alpine 3.24 received the fix in openssh-server 10.3_p1-r2.
  • For systems that cannot immediately upgrade, the article says disabling password authentication or using the PAM package with UsePAM yes blocked the bypass in testing.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access, pam, container-platform

Products: openssh, alpine-linux, musl-libc

Vendors: openssh, alpine-linux, musl

Turning Up the Heat: Inside the Attacks on Europe’s Refrigeration System — Should Read

Cyberattacks on internet-exposed refrigeration controllers disrupted hundreds of European supermarkets, raising units into defrost mode and causing widespread food spoilage, with France most heavily affected. The initial access method remains unconfirmed, but weak configurations, default credentials, and unpatched software are suspected.

  • Cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems in Europe since at least October 2026 placed controllers into defrost mode and caused supermarkets to discard spoiled food.
  • The first reported wave occurred on October 11–12, 2026 and primarily affected about 700 supermarkets in France, while a later wave on November 1–2 affected more than 100–115 retail locations across at least 10 additional European countries.
  • French authorities said refrigeration systems used by medical facilities were also affected, although there was no evidence that blood products were spoiled.
  • The initial access method is unconfirmed, but reporting has raised the possibility that vulnerable software or manufacturer-provided default credentials were involved.
  • Unit 42 identified more than 5,000 internet-exposed devices made by companies listed in a French CERT advisory, while noting that exposure did not establish that the devices were vulnerable.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device, ids-ips, xdr

Products: cortex-xpanse, device-security, advanced-threat-prevention, frontier-virtual-patching

Vendors: palo-alto-networks

French authorities probe cyberattack targeting nation’s blood supply — Should Read

French authorities are investigating a cyberattack on a refrigeration-equipment supplier to the French Blood Establishment, raising concerns about disruption to France’s civilian blood supply.

  • French authorities are investigating a cyberattack targeting a refrigeration-equipment supplier for the French Blood Establishment (EFS).
  • The EFS oversees France’s civilian blood supply.
  • The incident follows a wave of hacks targeting refrigeration systems at supermarkets across Europe.
  • Health-ISAC sent its U.S. members an advisory warning about the potential risk of attack, according to its chief security officer Errol Weiss.

Medical services company settles with 4 states over 2023 hack of sensitive patient records — Should Read

Perry Johnson Companies will pay $300,000 and implement major security reforms after a 2023 breach exposed sensitive health data of more than 13 million people, allegedly enabled by compromised employee credentials and a lack of multi-factor authentication. Failure to comply could trigger an additional $9.7 million penalty from four U.S. states.

  • Perry Johnson Companies agreed to pay $300,000 to settle claims brought by the attorneys general of Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, and Michigan over a March 2023 data breach.
  • The breach exposed sensitive records of more than 13 million people nationwide, including names, Social Security numbers, medical information, insurance details, and test results.
  • According to New York Attorney General Letitia James’s office, hackers accessed the company’s systems using an employee’s credentials while the company lacked multi-factor authentication.
  • The attackers allegedly remained in the systems for two months, and security software recorded their activity but did not alert the information security team because it was poorly configured.
  • The settlement requires security improvements including multi-factor authentication, encryption, password management, annual risk assessments, and data-handling controls; noncompliance could result in an additional $9.7 million payment.

Technologies: mfa

Vendors: perry-johnson-companies
